thread:
mina: FYI we're seeing a cascade after the OIDC client swap + cert rotation at ~04:11 UTC. Symptoms: partial SCIM failures (403) and mixed KMS decrypt errors (InvalidCiphertextException) for some token blobs. Some users got their roles removed and then re-added (flapping). Logs: 
```
2026-09-10T04:12:03Z scim-sync err="InvalidCiphertextException" token=tok-213 user=pierre@example.com
2026-09-10T04:12:04Z scim-sync http 403 PATCH /Users/213 -> {"error":"forbidden"}
2026-09-10T04:12:05Z idp error="invalid_audience" client=old-oidc-client assertion=asp-321
```
Anyone oncall? @ops-lead @lia-security

ash: I'm up. Quick checklist: did infra touch KMS aliases or rotate keys? Also confirm whether token metadata includes key-id or only alias. mina — paste deploy logs and the infra stage names.

mina: deploy infra-deploy-20260910-04: stages = [rotate-saml-cert, oidc-client-swap, alias-sync]. No explicit rekey recorded, but alias-sync shows CreateAlias/UpdateAlias events in CloudTrail around 04:11:58. Token schema currently stores only ciphertext + token_id (no key-id).

infra-automation: [AUDIT] event=UpdateAlias user=infra-automation alias=alias/scim-provisioner oldTarget=pk-7a2d newTarget=pk-4c9b time=2026-09-10T04:11:58Z id=alias-5544

lia-security: that alias repointing + lack of key-id in token metadata is a red flag. If some tokens encrypted earlier reference the old key (pk-7a2d) but alias now points to pk-4c9b, decrypts will fail with InvalidCiphertext. Also saw an idp invalid_audience error which suggests OIDC client misconfigured; the synced assertions may have been rejected by the IdP for some clients causing SCIM calls to fail. Both issues could explain partial failures.

ops-lead: immediate mitigations: 1) pause alias-sync and restore alias->old key if key still exists, 2) bump SCIM deprovision grace to 72h and pause prune, 3) flip SCIM auth to fallback-idp for the short window if possible, 4) add a temporary fallback alias list in provisioner config to try older aliases. Mina/ash — can you run 1 and 2 now?

mina: pausing alias-sync now. Command used: `aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/scim-provisioner-old --target-key-id pk-7a2d` (old key present and Enabled). Also bumped grace via deploy patch: `kubectl set env deployment/scim-provisioner SCIM_DEPROV_GRACE_HOURS=72 -n infra` and paused prune cronjob.

ash: after alias restore I'm seeing successful decrypts for older tokens and a couple of 200s on SCIM calls at 04:18:41Z: 
```
2026-09-10T04:18:41Z scim-sync http 200 PATCH /Users/213 user=pierre@example.com action=update
```
However, tokens minted between 04:11:50-04:12:10 when alias was switched are encrypted with pk-4c9b and won't decrypt against old key. We'll need a re-encrypt job for those or preserve both keys in the provisioner fallback list.

lia-security: post-incident actions: - never reuse an alias for a new CMK; require alias naming with version suffix (alias/scim-provisioner-v{ts}) - store explicit key-id in token metadata at encrypt time so decrypt uses the exact key, not alias resolution - add a CloudTrail alert for alias Delete/Update that pages security + oncall when production aliases change - add preflight to alias-sync to verify no active ciphertexts reference the alias (or run a quick decrypt smoke test) - require infra-automation PR approval by security when alias/key policy changes are proposed.

ops-lead: additional remediation: - add CI test that runs `aws kms get-key-policy` after rotation and validates runtime principals have kms:Decrypt; - add pipeline gating to abort if IdP/oidc client validation fails (prevent oidc swap continuing on invalid audiences); - add runbook steps for re-encrypt helper and token migration. Assign owners: @ash write re-encrypt script + add fallback alias logic, @lia-security own gating + alerting, @mina run user reconciliation and postmortem. ETA EOD.

ash: re-encrypt helper snippet I'll add to runbook (aws CLI pattern):
```bash
# decrypt with explicit key -> encrypt with new key
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cipher.bin --key-id pk-7a2d --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode > token_plain.bin
aws kms encrypt --key-id pk-4c9b --plaintext fileb://token_plain.bin --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > token_new_cipher.bin
```
We'll also update token storage to include `key_id` and `kek_alias` fields.

infra-automation: disabling alias-sync job and opening PR to change alias naming + add preflight checks. PR id=pr-4729.

sre-bot: [INCIDENT] service=scim-provisioner incident=INC-2026-0910-19 status=mitigated mitigated_by=mina mitigated_at=2026-09-10T04:24:07Z runbook=https://redwood.runbooks/internal/scim-provisioning-triage :white_check_mark:

mina: final status: provisioner healthy, decrypt errors resolved for restored tokens, queued re-encrypt for mixed-key tokens, paused alias automation until PR merges. Moving to postmortem — attaching logs and timeline. (reactions: :thumbsup: from ash, :eyes: from lia-security)
